outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed status evaluations mark solution_passed false with 9 of 145 samples passing. Both trajectories are single-agent implementations with local verification that did not generalize to the hidden evaluator. The most concrete visible implementation contrast is parallel's less-aligned None stderr path versus serial's explicit TypeError handling, but that contrast did not change the official relation.
parallel_contributors: Swarm mode was available but not used; the parent chose a direct implementation and therefore produced no parallel coordination boundary.
Local verification missed official failures and left a visible None stderr mismatch showing a Node stack-location line.
serial_contributors: Serial also used a direct local implementation and broader local tests, including explicit None error handling.
Despite that local coverage, the official evaluator still failed the serial artifact at the same 9/145 score.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel split repr, literal parsing, iterutils, multiplication, argparse, and entry into six files; serial combined value and repr handling in pytypes and multiplication in the entry file.
Parallel's None case check exposed a Node stack-location stderr line, while serial caught the error and printed a TypeError message.
Serial tested malformed input and unrecognized arguments in one later command; parallel focused on help and missing-argument normalization plus a separate None probe.
evaluator_effects: The allowed pair evidence includes only aggregate official results, not hidden per-case failure details, so exact evaluator-mismatch cases cannot be reconstructed from the mounted inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process comparison only, not an exclusive hidden-failure diagnosis
